done_when: A head commit that differs from its parent only in Forge's close records does not cancel the parent's CI run still in progress, and reuses its result when it finishes, so a record-only commit adds no full test run

Scale: Release the land queue place while parent CI runs
Gate: prove the running parent finishes and its result is reused
Simpler: undocumented pre-push wait → explain the choice

findings.body:
Gain 5, Work 3, Harm 3
Raise: Not done
Case: normal use - A CI repo runs several test groups while close saves its review. The aggregate `tests` check does not exist until the groups finish (`tests/test_close_waits_for_running_checks.py:33-37`), but this loop only recognizes exact configured check names. It therefore pushes immediately while groups are running; the generated workflow still cancels the parent (`src/forge/prcheck.py:52-54`), and reuse requires a completed successful workflow (`src/forge/templates/review-tests.py:125-127`). Single-job runs also get canceled when they remain busy after the 600-second deadline, including the 28-minute runs described in the issue. The `serious` check at `checks.py:129` likewise skips the wait for blocked-review record pushes, and unlisted longer-running workflows are not watched.
Done-when: A head commit that differs from its parent only in Forge's close records does not cancel the parent's CI run still in progress, and reuses its result when it finishes, so a record-only commit adds no full test run

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Scale
Case: normal use - On a four-core machine, `forge land --all` can have two independent closes waiting for their parents' running CI while a third waits to start. This new wait happens before `checks.wait` receives the queue's slot callback, so both closes retain their places for up to ten minutes. The existing wait lends a place during running checks (`src/forge/checks.py:232-234`), and the queue limits active places at `src/forge/land.py:516-519`; the new wait therefore delays independent work that previously could proceed.
Adds work: lend the existing queue place during the parent CI wait; F 2 x H 2 = 4; 2 x C = 4
findings.title: Scale: Release the land queue place while parent CI runs

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 2, Harm 2
Raise: Test
Case: normal use - Close saves a review while the code's CI is still running. This test sets the wait to zero, uses the fixture's already-green checks, and asserts only that a check-runs API lookup occurred before the push. It still passes if close reads the status once and pushes immediately, and it never checks cancellation or reuse. The existing reuse test supplies an already-completed parent, so it does not cover this transition. Exercise the command with a running parent that later succeeds and verify that the record head skips the suite.

why: Issue 1656: in CI-test repos, close pushes its review record commit a few minutes after the code, and that push cancels the code's own CI run in progress (concurrency cancel-in-progress). The parent then has no successful run, so .forge/review-tests.py cannot reuse it, and every record-only commit starts a full run again: 72% of one client's runs, about 28 minutes each.
